mainTopic: Washing rules for an אבל during שבעה, and where the fast-day prayer goes in the עמידה.
overview: The amud continues the laws of an אבל washing during שבעה. In the first version, רבא allows a mourner to wash in cold water. A ברייתא about a בוגרת is read as a challenge to him, but the גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about eye makeup and hair dye. A story about רבי יוסי בר חנינא washing in cold water is offered as support for רבא. It is pushed away as a special case of mourning after mourning, where a ברייתא allows some easing and רב חסדא sets its limits. In a second version, רבא forbids cold water, and the same sources are discussed again from that side. The final הלכה is that the whole body may not be washed at all, while face, hands and feet may be washed in cold water, and anointing is allowed only to remove dirt. The גמרא then turns to where an individual who fasts adds the fast-day prayer, and רב יצחק and רב ששת place it inside שומע תפלה. A ברייתא about 'eighteen and nineteen' starts a debate over how many ברכות the שליח ציבור says on each stage of the public fasts. That debate continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A grown girl may not make herself unattractive while mourning her father
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a בוגרת may not neglect her appearance during mourning for her father. This suggests that a נערה may.
steps.simpleTranslation: A grown girl is not allowed to make herself unattractive during the mourning days for her father. That means a younger girl is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to test רבא's ruling that a mourner may wash in cold water. It is setting up a challenge that the next lines will try to pull out of this source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בוגרת is old enough to get married, so she should not look neglected, because that could hurt her chances. The ברייתא's wording suggests that a נערה is allowed to neglect herself. The question is what kind of neglect the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: A grown girl, over twelve and a half, old enough to marry
A young girl, between twelve and twelve and a half
To make herself unattractive or neglected
This implies (an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: A grown girl is not permitted
to make herself unattractive
during the days of mourning for her father.
This implies that a young girl is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין הַבּוֹגֶרֶת רַשָּׁאָה לְנַוֵּול אֶת עַצְמָהּ
steps.raayaObject: Whether a mourner may wash in cold water
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a בוגרת mourning her father

steps.title: The ברייתא cannot be about hot water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is about washing. It then rules out hot water, because רב חסדא says a mourner may not even put a finger into hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא talking about washing? With what kind of water? If you say hot water, would a grown girl really be allowed to wash in it? But רב חסדא said a mourner may not even put his finger into hot water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא guesses that the ברייתא is about washing. It shows that the ברייתא cannot mean hot water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא allowed a בוגרת to wash in hot water, it would clash with רב חסדא's strict rule that a mourner may not touch hot water at all. So the hot-water reading is knocked out. That leaves only cold water as an option.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that... (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: Is it not about washing?
And with what kind of water?
If you say with hot water,
is a grown girl not allowed to neglect herself?!
phrases.notes: He means: would she really be allowed to wash in hot water? That's hard to accept.

phrases.english: But didn't רב חסדא say:
A mourner is forbidden to put
his finger into hot water!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו בִּרְחִיצָה, וּבְמַאי? אִילֵימָא בְּחַמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts working out what the ברייתא from step 1 means
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as allowing a בוגרת to wash in hot water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא forbids a mourner even a finger in hot water, so the ברייתא cannot allow hot-water washing.

steps.title: So the ברייתא must be about cold water
steps.stepSummary: Since hot water is ruled out, the ברייתא must mean cold water. That would mean ordinary mourners may not wash even in cold water, and only the בוגרת is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it about cold water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. The ברייתא must be letting only a בוגרת wash in cold water, which goes against רבא's ruling that any mourner may wash in cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only a בוגרת may wash in cold water, then a נערה, and mourners in general, may not. That would contradict רבא, who allows every mourner to wash in cold water.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about cold water?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hot water is ruled out, cold water is the only option left
steps.raayaObject: A mourner may not wash in cold water, except for a בוגרת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a בוגרת, read as being about cold water
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling (first version) that a mourner may wash in cold water all שבעה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hot water is ruled out by רב חסדא, so the ברייתא must mean cold water. If only a בוגרת may use cold water, an ordinary mourner may not, against רבא.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא is about eye makeup and hair dye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא is not about washing at all. It is about painting the eyes and dyeing the hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about eye makeup and hair dye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof by reading the ברייתא as being about cosmetics, not washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ברייתא is about makeup, it says nothing about cold-water washing. So this source no longer threatens רבא's ruling. The final הלכה on cold water comes in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Dyeing the hair or beautifying oneself

phrases.english: No, it is about eye painting and hair dyeing.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about a בוגרת is about makeup, so it proves nothing about washing in cold water.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא was about washing, but it can be about cosmetics.

steps.title: Support from רבי יוסי בר חנינא washing in cold water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to support the view that permits cold water. רבי יוסי בר חנינא's sons died, and he washed in cold water all שבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let's say this supports him: רבי אבא הכהן said in the name of רבי יוסי הכהן that once the sons of רבי יוסי בר חנינא died, and he washed in cold water all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to support the earlier view (רבא's) that a mourner may wash in cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great rabbi washed in cold water through all of שבעה. That seems to show it is allowed for any mourner.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבא, who allowed a mourner to wash in cold water.

phrases.english: as רבי אבא הכהן said
in the name of רבי יוסי הכהן:
It once happened that the sons died
of רבי יוסי בר חנינא,
and he washed in cold water all seven days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first source fails, a new source is tried, this time supporting permission
steps.raayaObject: A mourner may wash in cold water
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי יוסי בר חנינא

steps.title: That was a special case of mourning after mourning
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. רבי יוסי בר חנינא suffered one loss right after another, and that special situation allows some easing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: There, it was a case where his mourning periods came one right after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the story by saying it was an unusual case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His sons died one after another, so his mourning periods piled up. In such a case the rules are eased. So the story does not show that a regular mourner may wash in cold water.

keyTerms.meaning: His mourning periods came one right after another

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean cold water is forbidden. It only means this story cannot prove it is allowed in a normal case.

phrases.english: They say: There
it was when his mourning periods came one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם בְּשֶׁתְּכָפוּהוּ אֲבָלָיו זֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the story of רבי יוסי בר חנינא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story was a special case of back-to-back mourning, so it cannot teach about a normal mourner.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows easing when mourning periods pile up
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up the special-case answer. If one's mourning periods came one after another, he may lighten heavy hair with a razor and wash his clothes in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If his mourning periods came one after the other and his hair became heavy, he may lighten it with a razor, and he may wash his clothing in water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that back-to-back mourning really does allow easing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a mourner may not cut his hair or wash his clothes. When mourning periods pile up, the ברייתא allows both. This explains why רבי יוסי בר חנינא could wash in cold water.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: תְּכָפוּהוּ אֲבָלָיו זֶה אַחַר זֶה,
phrases.english: As it was taught: If his mourning periods came one after the other,
and his hair grew heavy, he may lighten it with a razor,
and he may wash his clothing in water.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: תְּכָפוּהוּ אֲבָלָיו זֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the special case used in step 6
steps.raayaObject: Back-to-back mourning allows some easing of the mourning rules

steps.title: רב חסדא sets the limits of the easing
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits the easing. Hair may be lightened with a razor but not scissors, and clothes washed with plain water but not with cleaning materials.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: With a razor, but not with scissors. With water, but not with natron, sand, or soapwort.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains how far the ברייתא's easing goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in the special case, the mourner still may not groom himself in the usual way. רב חסדא allows only a razor, not scissors, and only plain water, not cleaning materials like natron, sand or soap-plant. So the easing stays limited.

keyTerms.meaning: A cleaning plant used like soap

steps.whatToRemember: Even when mourning periods pile up, the easing is limited: a razor and plain water only.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
With a razor, but not with scissors;
in water, but not with natron,
nor with sand, nor with soap-plant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּתַעַר אֲבָל לֹא בְּמִסְפָּרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the limits of the ברייתא in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In back-to-back mourning, hair may be lightened only with a razor, not scissors, and clothes washed only with plain water, not with cleaning agents.

steps.title: Second version: רבא forbids even cold water
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבא rules that an אבל may not wash in cold water all שבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבא said: A mourner is forbidden to wash in cold water all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבא's opinion. In this version רבא is strict: even cold water is forbidden for an אבל during all of שבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion debated whether cold water is allowed. This version puts רבא clearly on the strict side. The next steps will test this stricter view.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion argued against the earlier one. It is another version of the same discussion, told with רבא on the strict side.

phrases.english: Some say: Rava said:
A mourner is forbidden to wash in cold water all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the debate about cold water for a mourner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not wash even in cold water for all of שבעה.

steps.title: Why is cold water worse than meat and wine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why washing is forbidden when an אבל is allowed meat and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about this from meat and wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא. An אבל is allowed to eat meat and drink wine, which are pleasures, so why forbid something small like cold water?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge compares two kinds of comfort. If the bigger pleasure of meat and wine is allowed, it seems strange to forbid the smaller comfort of cold water.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks why two similar cases are treated differently

phrases.english: What is different about this from meat and wine?
phrases.notes: An אבל is allowed to eat meat and drink wine, so the גמרא wonders why washing is stricter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's strict ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that cold water is forbidden all שבעה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Meat and wine are bigger pleasures and are allowed, so cold water should be allowed too.

steps.title: Meat and wine calm his distress
steps.stepSummary: Meat and wine are allowed because they ease the mourner's anxiety, not for pleasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he does it to relieve his anxiety.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: meat and wine are allowed for a different reason. They help a grieving person calm his fear and distress.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission for meat and wine is not about pleasure. It is a help for someone in emotional pain. Washing does not do that, so the comparison fails and רבא's ruling stands.

phrases.english: There, to relieve his anxiety
is why he does it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from meat and wine.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the reason behind each permission
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Meat and wine are allowed as pleasures, so washing should be allowed too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Meat and wine are allowed to ease distress, a reason that does not apply to washing.

steps.title: Trying to prove רבא from the ברייתא about the grown woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to show that the ברייתא about a בוגרת must be about cold water, which supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a ברייתא supports him? 'A grown woman may not make herself unattractive.' This implies a young woman may. What is this about? If hot water, how can a grown woman be allowed? רב חסדא said a mourner may not even put his finger in hot water! So it must be about cold water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove רבא's strict view from a ברייתא. Only a בוגרת may wash, so ordinary mourners may not wash even in cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets a בוגרת avoid looking neglected, which implies a נערה, like any mourner, must stay unwashed. It cannot mean hot water, since רב חסדא forbids even a finger in hot water. So it means cold water, and cold water is normally forbidden, just as רבא says.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it supports him?
To make unattractive, to neglect one's appearance

steps.confusionAlert: Read "permitted to make herself unattractive" as being allowed to stay unwashed like a regular mourner. The בוגרת is the one who gets the leniency.

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבא in this second version.

phrases.english: A grown woman is not permitted to make herself unattractive.
This implies a young girl is permitted!
In what? If you say in hot water:
Is a grown woman not permitted to go unwashed?!
phrases.notes: He means: could a grown woman really be allowed to wash in hot water? That seems impossible.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chisda say:
A mourner may not put his finger into hot water!
Rather, is it not about cold water?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבא from the challenge, the גמרא looks for a source to support him.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that cold water is forbidden all שבעה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that a בוגרת may not make herself unattractive, together with רב חסדא's ban on even a finger in hot water

steps.title: No, the ברייתא is about eye paint and hair dye
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails because the ברייתא is not about washing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is about painting the eyes and dyeing the hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof, the same way it did in the first version. The ברייתא talks about eye paint and hair dye, not washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is about makeup, it tells us nothing about cold water. So רבא's strict view loses this support, though it is not disproven.

keyTerms.meaning: Painting the eyes with eye paint

phrases.english: No, it is about painting the eyes and dyeing the hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected; רבא's ruling itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא is about washing, but it can be read as being about eye paint and hair dye.

steps.title: רב חסדא: no laundry all שבעה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns that an ordinary אבל may not do laundry for all of שבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This tells us that a mourner may not do laundry all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא draws a lesson from the way the גמרא just explained the ברייתא about the בוגרת as speaking of כיחול and פירכוס (רש״י: 'מדמוקמינן לה בכיחול ופירכוס הוא הדין לתכבוסת'). Only she is allowed those, and the same goes for laundry: an ordinary mourner may not launder all שבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only a בוגרת may use eye paint and hair dye during mourning, then an ordinary אבל may not, and laundry is treated the same way. The ban covers all seven days, not just the first few.

keyTerms.meaning: This tells us; introduces a lesson drawn from a source

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: This tells us,
phrases.notes: "This" points back to the way the גמרא just explained the ברייתא about the בוגרת as speaking of כיחול and פירכוס; the same goes for laundry.

phrases.english: A mourner is forbidden to do laundry all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the way the גמרא just explained the ברייתא about the בוגרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ordinary אבל may not do laundry for all of שבעה.

steps.title: The final הלכה on washing and anointing
steps.stepSummary: Whole body: no washing at all. Face, hands, feet: cold only. Anointing with oil: forbidden, unless to remove dirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: a mourner may not wash his whole body in hot or cold water all seven days. His face, hands, and feet: hot is forbidden, cold is allowed. Anointing with oil, even a tiny amount, is forbidden. But to remove dirt, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion with the practical הלכה for an אבל about washing and anointing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the whole body, the strict view wins: even cold water is forbidden. For face, hands, and feet, cold water is allowed. Anointing for comfort is forbidden, but anointing to clean off dirt is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: To anoint or rub with oil

steps.whatToRemember: Whole body: no washing, hot or cold. Face, hands, feet: cold yes, hot no. Oil: no, unless it is to remove dirt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for how an אבל washes during שבעה.

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא: אָבֵל אָסוּר לִרְחוֹץ כׇּל גּוּפוֹ
phrases.english: And the הלכה is: a mourner may not wash his whole body

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּחַמִּין וּבֵין בְּצוֹנֵן כׇּל שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.english: whether in hot water or in cold water, all seven days.
But his face, his hands, and his feet:
in hot water it is forbidden, in cold water it is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לָסוּךְ, אֲפִילּוּ כָּל שֶׁהוּא אָסוּר.
phrases.english: But anointing with oil, even a tiny amount, is forbidden.
And if it is to remove dirt, it is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole discussion about mourners with the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An אבל may not wash his whole body even in cold water all שבעה. Face, hands, and feet may be washed in cold water only. Anointing is forbidden unless it is to remove dirt.

steps.title: How do we mention the fast in prayer?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: how and where the fast-day prayer is said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prayer of a fast: how do we mention it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of mourners and asks a new question. How is the special fast-day prayer added to the עמידה? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the practical way to add a fast-day prayer. The answer will say who says it and where in the עמידה it goes.

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer of a fast day

phrases.english: The prayer of a fast: how do we mention it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from mourning to a new topic about fast-day prayer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How and where the fast-day prayer is added to the עמידה.

steps.title: Said between גואל and רופא
steps.stepSummary: An individual who took on a תענית says the fast-day prayer between גואל and רופא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה gave his son רב יצחק permission, and he taught: An individual who took a fast upon himself says the fast-day prayer. And where does he say it? Between 'Who redeems' and 'Who heals.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers through a public teaching by רב יצחק, son of רב יהודה. An individual fasting says the fast-day prayer, and it goes between the ברכה of גואל and the ברכה of רופא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two points are taught. First, even a single person who took on a fast says the special prayer. Second, it has a fixed place: after גואל ישראל and before רופא חולי עמו ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: He gave him permission or guided him to teach publicly
The ברכה ending 'Who heals the sick'

phrases.aramaic: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ, וּדְרַשׁ:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda gave his son Rav Yitzchak permission, and he taught publicly:
An individual who took a fast upon himself
prays the prayer of a fast.
And where does he say it?
Between "Who redeems" and "Who heals."
phrases.notes: These are two ברכות of the עמידה: גואל ישראל and רופא חולי עמו ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ, וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the fast-day prayer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An individual who took on a fast says the fast-day prayer between the ברכות of גואל and רופא.

steps.title: Can one person add a whole new blessing for himself?
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק attacks the previous answer. An individual cannot set up his own separate ברכה between גואל and רופא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק objects: Does an individual get to set up a blessing all for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק challenges the answer from Step 17, which placed the fast-day prayer between גואל and רופא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the prayer between גואל and רופא makes it look like a new, separate ברכה in the עמידה. רב יצחק argues that a single person, as opposed to a community, has no power to create a fixed ברכה of his own.

keyTerms.meaning: sets up a fixed, separate blessing

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak objects to it:
But does an individual establish a blessing for himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the placement given in Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that an individual says the fast-day prayer between גואל and רופא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A spot of its own between two ברכות makes it a separate ברכה, and an individual cannot create one.

steps.title: The fast-day prayer goes inside שומע תפלה
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק gives a new placement: the individual adds his fast-day prayer inside the ברכה of שומע תפלה. רב ששת says the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יצחק said: He says it in 'Who listens to prayer.' And רב ששת said the same: in 'Who listens to prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the old placement, רב יצחק offers his own: the prayer goes inside שומע תפלה. רב ששת agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שומע תפלה is a general ברכה asking that our prayers be accepted. Adding a request inside it does not create a new ברכה, so רב יצחק's objection no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who listens to prayer', the general blessing near the end of the weekday עמידה
and so too said, showing another אמורא agrees

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yitzchak said:
In "Who listens to prayer."
phrases.notes: He means the fast-day prayer is said inside this ברכה, without making a new one.

phrases.english: And so too Rav Sheshet said:
In "Who listens to prayer."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the Step 17 answer after the objection in Step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The individual says it as a separate ברכה between גואל and רופא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The individual includes it inside שומע תפלה, so no new ברכה is created.

steps.title: A ברייתא says one prays eighteen and the other nineteen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: the only difference between an individual and a community is that one prays eighteen ברכות and the other prays nineteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected from a ברייתא: The only difference between an individual and a community is that this one prays eighteen and that one prays nineteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב יצחק and רב ששת. This step only quotes the source; the next steps work out what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone prays nineteen ברכות on a fast, he has added a whole separate ברכה. The question will be who that 'someone' is. If it can be an individual, then an individual can set up his own ברכה.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
There is no difference between an individual and a community,
except that this one prays eighteen,
and that one prays nineteen.
phrases.notes: Nineteen means the regular ברכות plus one whole extra ברכה for the fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to challenge Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק and רב ששת's ruling that an individual cannot set up his own ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא may show that an individual on a fast says nineteen, meaning a separate ברכה.

steps.title: Who are the 'individual' and the 'community' in the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means. It tries reading 'community' as the שליח ציבור, but rejects that because the שליח ציבור on a fast says twenty-four, not nineteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'individual' and what is the 'community'? If you say 'individual' means a real individual and 'community' means the שליח ציבור, does he say nineteen? He says twenty-four!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the ברייתא is talking about. It tests the obvious reading and rules it out, which sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading is a regular person compared to the prayer leader. But on a public fast the leader adds six ברכות and says twenty-four, so the number nineteen does not fit him.

keyTerms.meaning: if you would say, used to test a possible reading
the prayer leader who prays on behalf of the community

phrases.english: What is "individual" and what is "community"?
If you say "individual" means an actual individual,
and "community" means the prayer leader,
are these nineteen?
They are twenty-four!
phrases.notes: On a public fast the leader adds six extra ברכות to the eighteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the meaning of the ברייתא quoted in Step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the 'individual' and 'community' in the ברייתא are
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not the plain individual against the שליח ציבור, because the leader says twenty-four

steps.title: So an individual can set up his own ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא means two individuals: one keeping a private fast (eighteen) and one keeping a public fast (nineteen). That would prove an individual can set up a ברכה for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what it means: The only difference between an individual who took on a private fast and an individual who took on a public fast is that this one prays eighteen and that one prays nineteen. Learn from this: an individual sets up a blessing for himself!
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out the simple reading, the גמרא gives a new reading of the ברייתא that proves the opposite of רב יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading both people are individuals. The one on a public fast says nineteen, so he adds a separate ברכה. That shows an individual can set up his own ברכה, against רב יצחק and רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, is it not so that
a private fast one person takes on
a public fast for the whole community

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין יָחִיד דְּקִבֵּל עָלָיו תַּעֲנִית יָחִיד
phrases.english: There is no difference between an individual who took upon himself an individual's fast
and an individual who took upon himself a communal fast,
except that this one prays eighteen,
and that one prays nineteen.
Learn from this:
An individual establishes a blessing for himself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge with the only reading left after Step 21
steps.raayaObject: That an individual may set up a separate ברכה for himself
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא read as comparing two individuals, one keeping a private fast and one keeping a public fast

steps.title: It is the prayer leader, during the first three fasts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The 'community' really is the שליח ציבור, and the ברייתא means the first three public fasts, when he says only nineteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really I can tell you it means the שליח ציבור. As for your difficulty that the שליח ציבור prays twenty-four: the ברייתא means the first three fasts, when there are not twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first reading, 'community' means the prayer leader, and answers the problem that knocked it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twenty-four ברכות are said only on the later, stricter fasts. On the first three fasts the leader adds just one ברכה, which makes nineteen. So the ברייתא is about the leader, and it does not prove that an individual may set up his own ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: really, I can tell you, used to defend the original reading
and as for what bothers you

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'nineteen' can be read as the שליח ציבור on the first three public fasts. That defends רב יצחק and רב ששת: an individual puts the fast-day prayer inside שומע תפלה. The next steps challenge the claim that the first three fasts lack the twenty-four ברכות.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא proves an individual adds a separate ברכה. Once it is read as the prayer leader on the first three fasts, it says nothing about individuals at all.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר,
phrases.english: No, really I can tell you it is the prayer leader,
and as for what is difficult for you:
that the prayer leader prays twenty-four,
it means the first three fasts,
when there are not twenty-four.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 22 by bringing back and defending the reading dropped in Step 21
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the leader always says twenty-four. On the first three fasts he says nineteen, so the ברייתא can mean the leader.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defense leaves רב יצחק and רב ששת's ruling in place: an individual puts the fast-day prayer inside שומע תפלה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the first and middle fasts differ only about work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 23 from a ברייתא. It says the only difference between the first three and middle three fasts is the ban on work, so the twenty-four ברכות should be the same for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true he doesn't say twenty-four on the first three fasts? The ברייתא says 'the only difference': the only difference between the first three fasts and the middle three is that on the first ones work is allowed and on the middle ones work is forbidden. That means about the twenty-four ברכות, both are the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 23, that the שליח ציבור says only nineteen ברכות on the first three fasts. It quotes a ברייתא that lists only one difference between the first and middle fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "אין בין" mean "the ONLY difference is." If work is the only difference, then everything else must be equal, including the twenty-four ברכות. So if the twenty-four are said on the middle fasts, they should also be said on the first three, and Step 23's answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: "There is no difference between... except": the only difference is
The first three public fasts for rain

steps.confusionAlert: The rain fasts come in three stages: the first three, the middle three, and the last seven. The argument here assumes the twenty-four ברכות are said on the middle fasts.

phrases.english: And not?
phrases.notes: He means: is it really true the שליח ציבור doesn't say twenty-four on the first three fasts?

phrases.english: But it teaches "there is no difference between":
The difference between the first three fasts
and the middle three fasts
is only that on these, they are permitted to do work,
and on these, they are forbidden to do work.
This implies that regarding the twenty-four ברכות
this and that are the same!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 23, that the first three fasts have only nineteen ברכות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the שליח ציבור says only nineteen on the first three fasts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "אין בין" means work is the only difference between the first and middle fasts, so the twenty-four ברכות must apply to both.

steps.title: The ברייתא taught some differences and left some out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא's list is not complete. The difference in prayers was simply left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא taught some things and left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא did not list every difference. The difference about the twenty-four ברכות is one it skipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a common answer in the גמרא: a list does not have to be complete. If so, the ברייתא does not prove the prayers are the same on both kinds of fasts.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught some and left some out: the list is not complete

phrases.english: He taught and he left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The list in the ברייתא is not complete.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists every difference, so the prayers must be the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא skipped the difference in prayers.

steps.title: Two problems with saying the list is incomplete
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects "he left some out." Nothing else was left out, and the words "אין בין" mean the list is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: What else did he leave out, that we should say he left this out too? And also: it says 'the only difference'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two reasons why "he left some out" does not work here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First: we usually say a list skipped items only if we can point to another skipped item, and here there is none. Second: the words "אין בין" openly say this is the only difference, so the list cannot be partial.

keyTerms.meaning: What else did he leave out, that this one was left out?

phrases.english: What else did he leave out, that you say he left out this?
phrases.notes: We only say a list skipped something if we can find another thing it skipped too.

phrases.english: And furthermore: it teaches "there is no difference between"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the answer of Step 25.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing else was left out, and "אין בין" says the list is complete.

steps.title: The ברייתא only discusses prohibitions, not prayers
steps.stepSummary: New answer: the ברייתא only compares what is forbidden on the fasts. It is not talking about prayers at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תנא is talking about prohibitions; he is not talking about prayers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a better answer. The ברייתא's "only difference" covers only the prohibitions of the fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside its topic, the prohibitions, the list is complete, so "אין בין" is still exact. Prayers are a different topic, so the ברייתא tells us nothing about the twenty-four ברכות.

phrases.english: Rather, the תנא is speaking about prohibitions;
about prayers he is not speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 25 with a new answer to Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the topic of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "אין בין" covers every kind of difference, including prayers.
steps.terutzMaskana: "אין בין" covers only prohibitions, so prayers can differ.

steps.title: Or: even the middle fasts have no twenty-four ברכות
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: the middle three fasts also do not have twenty-four ברכות. So the first and middle fasts really are the same in prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: on the middle fasts too, he does not pray twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer Step 24. The twenty-four ברכות are not said on the middle fasts either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we agree the ברייתא makes the first and middle fasts equal in prayer. But that is no problem, because both have only nineteen. The twenty-four would then belong only to the last seven fasts.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: a second answer

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
on the middle fasts too
he does not pray twenty-four.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּאֶמְצָעֲיָיתָא נָמֵי לָא מְצַלֵּי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the קשיא of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the assumed law about the middle fasts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The middle fasts have twenty-four, so the first three should too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The middle fasts also have only nineteen, so the ברייתא is fine.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: the middle fasts equal the last seven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the second answer. Another ברייתא says the middle three and last seven fasts differ only in the alarm and closing stores, so the twenty-four should be said on the middle fasts too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really so? But a ברייתא teaches: the only difference between the second three fasts and the last seven is that on the last ones they sound the alarm and lock the stores. That means in everything else, both are the same! And if you say here too he taught some and left some out, it says 'the only difference'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 28 with a second ברייתא. It also blocks the escape "he left some out" in advance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last seven fasts surely have twenty-four ברכות. If the middle three differ from them only in the alarm and the stores, then the middle three must also have twenty-four. That goes against Step 28.

keyTerms.meaning: The second set of three fasts (the middle ones)
They sound the alarm (blow and cry out)

phrases.english: And not?!
phrases.notes: He means: do the middle fasts really not have twenty-four?

phrases.english: But it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין שָׁלֹשׁ שְׁנִיּוֹת לְשֶׁבַע אַחֲרוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: The difference between the second three and the last seven
is only that on these they sound the alarm
and lock the stores.
This implies that regarding all their other matters
this and that are the same!

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר
phrases.english: And if you say that here too he taught and left out,
but it teaches "there is no difference between"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין בֵּין שָׁלֹשׁ שְׁנִיּוֹת לְשֶׁבַע אַחֲרוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second answer (Step 28), using the same "אין בין" reasoning as Steps 24 and 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the middle fasts have no twenty-four ברכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The middle fasts equal the last seven in everything except the alarm and stores, so they share the twenty-four ברכות. "אין בין" blocks the answer "he left some out."

steps.title: Is "the only difference" really meant exactly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the whole argument. It asks whether "אין בין" is really meant as a complete list, setting up the next move.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do you really think 'the only difference' is meant exactly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the base of the last challenge: maybe "אין בין" does not really mean "the only difference." This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא will show the ברייתא leaves out other differences.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 26 and 29 both stood on the idea that "אין בין" means a complete list. If that is not true, the answer "he left some out" works again, and the challenge from the second ברייתא goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so?

phrases.english: And can you really think that "there is no difference between" is meant exactly?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to reject the challenge of Step 29 by attacking its starting point.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea, used in Steps 26 and 29, that "אין בין" must mean a complete list.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: "אין בין" may not be meant exactly, so the list can still have items left out.
